datasets.name: Renewables.ninja hourly PV output (MERRA-2), 1 kWp reference system
datasets.publisher: Renewables.ninja (Pfenninger & Staffell; Imperial College London / ETH Zurich)
datasets.geography: Paris, France (lat 48.85, lon 2.35), tilt 35 deg, south, losses 10%
datasets.license: Renewables.ninja states CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial, attribution); verify at https://www.renewables.ninja/about. Anonymous API access, no account created.
datasets.preprocessing: Parsed from the JSON API response, clipped to [0,1] kW/kWp, converted from UTC to Europe/Paris local time.
datasets.role: Actual on-site PV generation = capacity factor x installed kWp x scenario scale.

datasets.name: ELMAS: hourly electrical load profiles of French industrial and tertiary sectors (18 clusters, 2018)
datasets.publisher: Bellinguer, Girard, Bocquet, Chevalier (MINES Paris - PSL / Enedis); Scientific Data 10, 2023
datasets.units: average energy per hour per cluster (normalised to mean 1 here: only the SHAPE is used)
datasets.resolution: hourly, one year (2018), averaged over 55,730 customers
datasets.preprocessing: Decimal commas parsed; each cluster divided by its annual mean; timestamps shifted by 364 days so 2018 weekdays/seasons align with the 2019 calendar; clusters [1, 10] used for training scenarios, [14, 11] held out for an OOD family.
datasets.role: Shape of the plant's inflexible load (base_kw_mean x shape). Absolute plant size is an assumption.

datasets.name: Day-ahead spot price, bidding zone FR
datasets.publisher: Fraunhofer ISE Energy-Charts API; data from Bundesnetzagentur | SMARD.de
datasets.license: CC BY 4.0 (stated in the API response: 'CC BY 4.0 from Bundesnetzagentur | SMARD.de')
datasets.preprocessing: Resampled to hourly mean, /1000, local time. Negative prices kept in the spot series; the customer tariff is floored at 0.
datasets.role: Wholesale component of the tariff (tariff = spot x scale + network adder + levies).

datasets.name: Public net electricity generation by source, France
datasets.class: derived from public data + literature factors
datasets.resolution: hourly/15 min, resampled to hourly mean
datasets.license: Energy-Charts states CC BY 4.0 for its data (the response carries no licence field; verify at https://www.energy-charts.info).
datasets.preprocessing: Per-source MW averaged hourly; null/negative -> 0; carbon intensity = sum(generation x emission factor) / sum(generation). Imports/exports and pumped-storage charging excluded (production-based).
datasets.role: Time-varying grid carbon intensity (gCO2e/kWh); France is nuclear-dominated so the level is low (about 54 g/kWh mean).

datasets.name: Emission factors per generation technology
datasets.publisher: IPCC AR5 WGIII (2014) Annex III, Table A.III.2 (median lifecycle): coal 820, gas CCGT 490, biomass 230, geothermal 38, hydro 24, nuclear 12, solar PV utility 48, onshore wind 11, offshore wind 12 gCO2e/kWh
datasets.license: IPCC reports: free for non-commercial use with citation
datasets.preprocessing: Lignite (1000), oil (650), coal-derived gas (600), waste (400), others (500) are ANALYST ASSUMPTIONS (not IPCC values) - see config/default.yaml.
datasets.role: Convert the generation mix into carbon intensity.

datasets.name: TURPE 7 HTA network tariff, variable energy component (grid of 1 Aug 2025)
datasets.class: published regulated tariff (transcribed by hand into config/default.yaml)
datasets.publisher: Commission de regulation de l'energie (CRE), deliberation no 2025-40 of 4 Feb 2025
datasets.units: c EUR/kWh for the five ranges PTE, HPH, HCH, HPE, HCE; options CU (short) and LU (long utilisation)
datasets.resolution: five time ranges (fixed peak Dec-Feb; high season Nov-Mar, low season Apr-Oct; full vs off-peak hours)
datasets.license: Public regulatory document (CRE); cite the deliberation
datasets.preprocessing: Values copied from the 'Grilles simplifiees de la composante de soutirage au 1er aout 2025' table (CU 5.85/4.31/2.03/1.03/0.71, LU 2.71/2.14/1.50/0.94/0.69 c/kWh). Off-peak placement A = 22-06 h and Sundays (CRE text); placement B = low-season off-peak 02-06 h + 11-15 h (derived from CRE Table 47 'hours to favour' 02-06 h and 11-17 h; 8 h/day). Exact fixed-peak hours 09-11 h and 18-20 h are an ASSUMPTION inside the CRE windows (08-12 h, 17-21 h). The 2026 +3.04 % indexation and the power (EUR/kW/yr) components are not applied, except that the CU power term 14.70 EUR/kW/yr/365 is used as the daily demand charge. Supply margin, accise and CTA (0.03 EUR/kWh) are assumed, not sourced.
datasets.role: Network part of the electricity price: gives the peak / intermediate / off-peak structure. NOTE: tariff year (2025-26) differs from the market data year (2019); the wholesale price is used as a level-shifting signal.

datasets.name: Production jobs, deadlines, forecast errors, PV drops, plant size
datasets.preprocessing: Generated by energyrl/scenarios.py from seeded random draws; ELMAS gives only the base-load shape, not job schedules.
datasets.role: Flexible loads: job power, durations, release times, deadlines.
